title: on-demand-econ-telemetry-gating-for-cold-batches
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Cold-start prefill and aggressive batching can save tokens but occasionally regresses latency or tail SLOs for bursty tenants. This change introduces an on-demand economic telemetry gate that uses recent unit-econ signals (cost-per-inference, cache-hit-rate, tail-latency anomaly score) to decide whether to allow prefill/batching optimizations for a tenant in the next 60s window. The gate is conservative by default and only flips to permissive when telemetry crosses heuristics derived from historical tenant profiles.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a telemetry-driven gating layer between the request router and the prefill/batcher pipeline, implements a lightweight running-window unit-econ scorer, extends the runtime config model with tenant_econ_policy and fallback_quant_profile, adds a dry-run CLI mode to simulate gate decisions, and wires metrics and logs to the Console dashboards.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1442), [x] unit tests for scorer, [x] integration test exercising gate decision against synthetic bursts, [x] dashboards updated, [x] backward-compatible config defaults, [x] documentation snippet in runtime/README.

Design notes and links: The gate uses three signals: normalized_cost_delta (tokens/cost drift vs baseline), cache_hit_rate_ewma (50s window), and tail_latency_z (90th-99th zscore). We compute a weighted score and compare to tenant thresholds that are auto-derived (see design doc). If the gate denies prefill, the router falls back to a minimally-batched fast-path and an optional lower-quant profile (fallback_quant_profile) that prioritizes latency. Implementation choices emphasize safety: thresholds require 2 consecutive positive windows to enable aggressive prefill, and an emergency override exists for operator lock-in. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1442/telemetry-gating-for-cold-batches and runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cost-gate-runbook.

Commit summary: - introduce econ/gate package with scorer and policy types - runtime: add tenant config and gating hook into request router - batcher: expose prefill_enable_hint and fast-path execution - cli: add gate-simulate dry-run with sample traces - console: add minimal metrics (tenant_gate_decision, econ_score_components) - tests: unit and integration harness updates

Files changed (high level): - runtime/router/gate.go: new gate integration and feature flag checks - econ/scorer/scorer.go: running-window scorer and tests - batcher/prefill_hint.go: hint plumbing to respect gate decision - config/tenant_policy.yaml: new defaults and example tenant override - cli/gate_simulate.go: dry-run mode to replay traces and print decisions - console/metrics/telemetry_defs.yaml: metric definitions + panel links - tests/integration/gate_integration_test.go: synthetic burst scenarios

Behavior and safety: The default tenant_econ_policy is conservative: gate is opt-in per-tenant, and global default is disabled for free-tier tenants. The change introduces no forced quant changes; fallback_quant_profile is an explicit tenant config that admins can set. The gate is feature-flagged (runtime.feature_flags.enable_econ_gate) and initially off for all clusters.

Observability: New metrics: tenant_econ_score_total (gauge), tenant_gate_decision{tenant,decision}, tenant_cache_hit_rate_ewma, tenant_cost_delta_norm. Logs include structured events when a gate flips state and when fallback quant is applied. Dashboards and alert rules added under Console > Prefill Safety > Econ Gates.

Testing notes: Local unit tests exercise scorer weight combinations and edge windows. Integration harness replays recorded traces and asserts that tail latency degradation does not increase >1% when gate denies prefill. Load tests on benchmark-lab show median latency improvement for permissive tenants ~6% and unit-cost reduction ~8% for batched flows.

How to review: Focus areas are scorer correctness, router integration race conditions, and telemetry cardinality for metrics. Suggested reviewers: runtime for router changes, infra for metrics cardinality, and who owns batcher behavior.

Related work: ties to ENG-1463 (batch-safety-playbook) and earlier work on tenant-warming (pr-457321). This implementation intentionally separates econ gating from the autoscaler and from quota enforcement to avoid permission coupling.

Merge strategy: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Carlos Vega (2026-02-19): Can we avoid a hot-path allocation in router ShouldAllowPrefill? Suggest reusing request context buffer. Also please add a microbenchmark to guard against per-request overhead.
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): @carlos good catch — updated gate.go to use request.Context metadata pool and added microbench under runtime/benchmarks/gate_bench_test.go

Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Exposed tenant override in config schema and added explanatory comments and unit test for zscore computation. Kept default conservative as requested.
Ethan Walsh (2026-02-23): Integration tests flaky once (timeout). CI rerun resolved it. Approving after green CI.

release_notes: Add telemetry-driven tenant econ gating to selectively enable/disable prefill and aggressive batching per tenant. Introduces tenant_econ_policy config, a running-window econ scorer, and a CLI dry-run to simulate decisions. Feature gated off by default.
